rationale: Build the room and viewpoint first, then establish the central island and surrounding cabinetry before adding joinery and refining the wood appearance. Use each actual render to check framing, visibility, proportions, and tonal separation; record obscured or uncertain details for later review.

stages.title: Room and viewpoint
stages.completed_scope: A simple room shell, wood-toned floor, camera, and lighting establish the reference viewpoint and composition.

stages.title: Central work island
stages.completed_scope: The large rectangular wood countertop and its darker supporting cabinet establish the central silhouette, overhang, and floor contact.

stages.title: Perimeter cabinetry
stages.completed_scope: The tall glazed cabinet on the left and the upper and lower cabinetry along the right wall establish the surrounding furniture arrangement.

stages.title: Cabinet joinery
stages.completed_scope: Visible cabinet divisions, recessed panels, glazed door frames, handles, and base trim make the furniture groups recognizable while preserving their established proportions.

stages.title: Appearance and global check
stages.completed_scope: Wood tones and surface variation distinguish the countertop, cabinetry, and floor; a final render checks framing, visibility, contacts, and tonal readability across the completed scene, with obscured details recorded as uncertain.
